title: Per-case staff-time and activity-log records for my open PRAs
summary:
Meta-request for the existing records by which the Department and the City track, log, and attribute staff time and case activity to specific PRA case numbers. SMPD has characterized the requester's PRAs as requiring substantial staff time — including a figure of approximately 10 hours — and this request seeks the records that any such figure would be derived from.

In scope: 32 PRA case numbers from W012129-020926 through W012742-051426.

Records requested:

- Item 1: per-case activity / audit logs from the PRA management platform (GovQA or equivalent), including every logged entry with timestamp, action, and associated user.
- Item 2: per-case staff-time / labor attribution records (reports, dashboard views, spreadsheets, internal memos) attributing hours or labor cost to specific PRA case numbers.
- Item 3: timesheet / labor-distribution records coding hours to 'Public Records' / 'CPRA' / equivalent project, task, or case-number codes, linkable to the case numbers in scope. If the time-tracking system records hours at project- or department-aggregate level rather than per case, that aggregate-level record is responsive.
- Item 4: internal communications among Department or City staff (City Attorney, City Clerk, Records Unit, Department supervisors) referencing time required, anticipated, or expended on the case numbers in scope.
- Item 5: SOPs / written guidelines / training material governing how staff are expected to log, track, code, or attribute staff time to PRAs, and any document describing the PRA-management-system case-note / activity-log / time-tracking configuration.

policy_promises.policy: Gov. Code § 7922.530 / Sierra Club v. Superior Court (2013) 57 Cal.4th 157
policy_promises.tests: Are the per-case activity logs, time-attribution records, and timesheet entries in scope existing routine system exports, not compilation?

policy_promises.policy: City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608
policy_promises.quote: records held by a vendor on the agency's behalf are agency records
policy_promises.tests: If GovQA / a SaaS timekeeping platform holds the responsive records on the City's behalf, those records are subject to production.

policy_promises.quote: any reasonably segregable portion of a record
policy_promises.tests: Can per-case hour-attribution data be produced with employee-identifier columns redacted, or is the entire record withheld on personnel-privacy grounds?
Are per-case hour-attribution columns 'personnel records' within the meaning of the exemption?

Most recent case number in the request's 32-PRA scope list at filing.

filed_because: SMPD has characterized the requester's PRAs as a substantial workload (the ~10-hours figure). This request asks for the existing records by which any such characterization would be supported — per-case activity logs, time attribution, and timesheet coding — so workload claims can be assessed against the underlying data rather than the agency's narrative.
notes:
Initial determination received 2026-06-04 (rolling production). Per-item disposition: Item 3 (timesheet / labor-distribution coding) — no responsive records; Item 4 (internal communications referencing staff time) — withheld in full after City Attorney legal review under § 7922.525(b), on attorney-client privilege per § 7927.705 / Evidence Code § 954; Item 5 (time-tracking SOPs) — one responsive record produced (Public-Records-Act-Procedures.pdf). Items 1-2 (per-case activity logs, labor-attribution records) in rolling production: initial batch released, City committed to a further update no later than 2026-06-18.

Note the tension: Item 3's 'no responsive records' answer asserts no per-case or aggregate 'Public Records' time coding exists, even as Items 1-2 produce per-case PRA activity logs — so the ~10-hour workload figure SMPD attributed to these requests has no disclosed labor-attribution record behind it.

Closed 2026-06-17 (Juliana Santiago). Final per-item disposition: Item 1 (per-case activity / audit logs) produced — 30 per-case GovQA Audit_History PDFs uploaded, with portions withheld under § 7927.705 / Evidence Code § 954; Item 2 (per-case staff-time / labor-attribution records) withheld in full under § 7927.705 / Evidence Code § 954 and CCP § 2018.030 (attorney work product); Item 3 (timesheet / labor coding) no responsive records; Item 4 (internal communications referencing staff time) withheld in full after City Attorney review under § 7927.705 / Evidence Code § 954; Item 5 produced 2026-06-04. The 2026-06-10 requester follow-up pressing how the ~10-hours-per-week figure (W012462 5/5 letter) and the 211,872-document figure were derived, and whether any non-attorney internal communication discussed them, was met by closure under privilege without a separate derivation answer — Item 3 = none and Item 2 = withheld as privileged/work-product, so no labor-attribution record behind the ~10-hour figure was disclosed.
